research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK/DSIT/DESNZ/MHCLG, Defra and Ofgem material checked on 25 July 2026. AI Growth Zone application criteria, data-centre planning reforms, strategic electricity-demand connection proposals, critical-infrastructure status, Section 35 directions and future NSIP BNG remain at their published programme, consultation, regulatory or project-procedure scope. They are not parcel power capacity, water capacity, planning permission, DCO grant, operational resilience certification or Future Growth score accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification; AIGZ selection criteria, planning status, grid connection, water evidence, Section 35/DCO procedure, CNI regulation and future BNG date kept separate; repository collision check before publication.

source_facts.fact: The published application guidance asks sites to demonstrate at least 500MW of power capacity by 2030, water sufficient to support at least 500MW of AI infrastructure, and at least 100 acres of land available by 2028.
source_facts.gate: Application thresholds are eligibility/evidence criteria and not proof a parcel currently has those capacities or planning permission.

source_facts.fact: Government policy identifies power access and planning as core barriers and describes measures to accelerate AI data-centre delivery.
source_facts.gate: Programme support is not a project consent or connection agreement.

source_facts.fact: The March 2026 consultation proposes prioritisation reforms for strategic electricity demand including data centres.
source_facts.gate: Consultation proposals must not be represented as final implemented connection rights.

source_facts.fact: A June 2026 factsheet says data centres were designated critical national infrastructure in 2024 and sets out proposed essential-service regulation for qualifying operators.
source_facts.gate: CNI or essential-service status is not planning permission or site suitability.

source_facts.fact: Defra's data-centre biodiversity gain statement says NSIP BNG becomes mandatory from 2 November 2026.
source_facts.gate: The future effective date must not be backdated to 25 July 2026.

source_facts.fact: On 1 July 2026 the Secretary of State issued a Section 35 direction for a proposed Dartford data-centre campus to use the Planning Act DCO regime.
source_facts.gate: Section 35 direction is not a DCO grant or construction approval.

core_rules: AI Growth Zone designation is not planning permission
AI Growth Zone application is not designation
programme support is not a land-use consent
500MW application criterion is not current site power capacity
500MW target must not be inferred from grid proximity
connection agreement evidence and available capacity must remain distinct
strategic-demand policy proposal is not a connection offer
consultation proposal is not final implemented regulation
network prioritisation does not guarantee energisation date
power capacity must not be fabricated from substation distance
water criterion is not proof water supplier capacity exists
supplier confirmation must be project-specific
water availability and wastewater discharge must remain distinct
water infrastructure timeline is not planning permission
100-acre criterion is not a parcel-size planning threshold
land availability is not ownership unless evidenced
ownership is not planning permission
site control is not construction readiness
AI data-centre policy support is not project approval
data-centre planning reform consultation is not adopted policy unless confirmed
draft NPPF text must not be treated as current adopted NPPF
Section 35 direction is not development consent
Section 35 direction only selects Planning Act treatment for the project concerned
DCO application is not DCO grant
DCO grant is not construction commencement
data-centre NSIP route and local planning route must remain distinct
CNI designation is not planning consent
essential-service regulation is not building-safety certification
cyber-resilience requirement is not land-use suitability
operational resilience is not grid resilience proof
data-centre energy study is not site demand forecast
national data-centre energy demand must not be downscaled to a parcel
AI Growth Zone electricity discount proposal is not a current universal tariff right
future pricing support must retain its effective-date conditions

network investment plan is not completed network reinforcement
AI Energy Council discussion is not a binding consent
economic investment announcement is not delivered infrastructure
jobs forecast is not planning evidence

NSIP BNG date must not be backdated before 2 November 2026
BNG requirement is not DCO approval
BNG statement does not establish a site's biodiversity baseline
data-centre cooling technology must not be guessed
water consumption must not be inferred from MW alone
NO_DATA must not become no data-centre infrastructure constraint
research confidence is not parcel data-centre viability accuracy
